metadata.title: Claude Code, Hook Development.
metadata.purpose: Answer whether getting Claude Code to automatically stop or react to something is a thing you ask for in conversation or a thing you configure, using the hook-development skill's own PreToolUse block on .env writes as the concrete case. Lands the carry-out that a hook is a script wired to one exact event, not a request you make in conversation.
metadata.anchor_pair: B02 -> B03 (the PreToolUse hook blocking .env writes: fires reliably in the right config shape, silently doesn't in the wrong one)

beats.narration_text: Someone asks Claude Code to just remember to skip the dot-env file. But a reminder can slip. The real fix is a hook — a script tied to one exact moment. What's inside one?

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'How do I set a reminder for Claude Code to skip my .env file?', hesitates on 'reminder', corrects to 'hook', lands the real question

props.text:
How do I set a reminder
for Claude Code

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('reminder' -> 'hook') is visible on a late frame.

beats.narration_text: A reminder lives inside the conversation — once the context scrolls away or a new session starts, it's gone. A hook lives in a config file that Claude Code reads before it acts, whether or not those words are still nearby. It fires at fixed moments — nine of them — from before a tool runs to when a session starts or ends.

shot.new_visual_element: A reminder bubble scattering as conversation text scrolls past; beside it a config file staying fixed; nine tick marks lighting along a timeline

production_viz.label: A file, not a memory
production_viz.mechanic: Left: a speech-bubble labelled 'reminder' fades and scatters as lines of conversation scroll upward past it. Right: a file icon labelled 'hooks.json' stays fixed and solid while the same conversation scrolls behind it, unaffected. Beneath both, a horizontal line with nine tick marks lights up left to right; two are named directly — 'before a tool runs' under the first, 'session starts / ends' under the last two.

beats.narration_text: Two ways to write a hook. A command hook is a bash script — the same deterministic check, every time. A prompt-based hook hands the decision to Claude's own judgment instead. Watch PreToolUse handle the dot-env case: before any tool runs, it checks the file path, and returns one of three answers — allow, deny, or ask — stopping the write before it happens.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR — PreToolUse checking a write to .env, branching to allow / deny / ask, deny firing and the write struck

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR — PreToolUse checks, then blocks
production_viz.mechanic: Two cards side by side fade in: 'command' (a terminal glyph, 'bash script, same check every time') and 'prompt-based' (a thought-glyph, 'Claude's judgment'). THE ANCHOR. Both cards shrink to the top; below, a PreToolUse box receives a write attempt to '.env', branches to three labelled outcomes — allow, deny, ask — and 'deny' lights up in terracotta while a strike mark lands over the attempted write. THIS EXACT SEQUENCE RETURNS AT B03.

beats.narration_text: Get the shape right and that block fires every single time — reliable, because a hook doesn't forget. But there are two ways to write the config, and they're not interchangeable: a plugin's hooks.json wraps its events inside a hooks key; a project's settings.json puts those same events directly at the top level. Swap the shapes and the hook doesn't error — it simply never fires, and nothing tells you why.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — the same deny firing three times reliably, then two config shapes side by side, the swapped one fading to silence with no error

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — reliable, then silently wrong
production_viz.mechanic: THE B02 DENY SEQUENCE RETURNS, identical, and fires three times in a row — each marked teal 'blocked'. Then two file shapes appear side by side: a wrapped object reading '{ hooks: { PreToolUse: [...] } }' labelled 'plugin hooks.json', and a flat object reading '{ PreToolUse: [...] }' labelled 'settings.json'. The wrapped shape is dragged into the settings.json slot; the PreToolUse box beneath goes dark — no strike mark, no error text, just silence — labelled 'never fires'.

beats.narration_text: A hook isn't something you ask Claude to remember — it's a script wired to one exact moment, and it fires exactly as configured, or not at all.

props.quote: A hook isn't something you ask Claude to remember — it's a script wired to one exact moment, and it fires exactly as configured, or not at all.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. Create a PreToolUse hook for my plugin that blocks writes to dot-env files and system paths. Watch three things when Claude answers: does hooks.json wrap the event inside a hooks key, the way a plugin's config needs, instead of sitting directly at the top level the way a project's settings.json would? Does the script path use dollar CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT instead of a hardcoded path, so the hook still works once the plugin moves? And is there a timeout set, instead of leaning on the sixty-second default? Liam, in for Bear.
